extractionRules: Every claim is a verbatim-supported statement from a retrieved structured abstract.
No inference beyond the source; associations not converted to causation; populations not broadened.
IBD-general (UC+Crohn's) consensus content is labelled ibd_general and NOT relabelled UC-specific.
All claims are pending_clinical_review; no claim is approved.

claims.normalizedClaim: In people with ulcerative colitis in symptomatic remission, the AGA guideline panel suggests a monitoring strategy that combines a non-invasive biomarker with symptoms rather than symptoms alone.
claims.exactSupportingExcerpt: In patients with UC in symptomatic remission, the panel suggests the use of a biomarker- and symptom-based monitoring strategy over a symptom-based monitoring strategy.
claims.exactLocator: Abstract (structured), Results section — Europe PMC record EXT_ID:36822736; Gastroenterology 2023;164(3):344-372. Page/statement-level locators require full text (link_only).
claims.sampleSize: Not reported in retrieved abstract (guideline / consensus synthesis)
claims.interventionOrExposure: Combined biomarker (fecal calprotectin / fecal lactoferrin / CRP) plus symptom monitoring
claims.limitations: Conditional recommendation; the guideline does not specify monitoring frequency in the retrieved abstract. Applies to established UC, not diagnosis.
claims.conflictsWithExistingEvidence: Consistent in direction with STRIDE-II (SRC-033), which lists normalisation of fecal/serum markers as a short-term target; STRIDE-II does not itself mandate a combined strategy.
claims.regionalApplicabilityNote: US (AGA). Transfers to Canada; assay availability and calibration differ.

claims.normalizedClaim: For a person with ulcerative colitis in symptomatic remission, the panel suggests using fecal calprotectin below 150 micrograms per gram, a normal fecal lactoferrin, and/or a normal CRP to rule out active inflammation and avoid routine endoscopic assessment.
claims.exactSupportingExcerpt: For patients in symptomatic remission, the panel suggests using fecal calprotectin <150 μg/g, normal fecal lactoferrin, and/or normal CRP to rule out active inflammation and avoid routine endoscopic assessment of disease.
claims.exactLocator: Abstract (structured), Results section — Europe PMC record EXT_ID:36822736; Gastroenterology 2023;164(3):344-372. Page/statement-level locators require full text (link_only).
claims.sampleSize: Not reported in retrieved abstract (guideline / consensus synthesis)
claims.interventionOrExposure: Fecal calprotectin <150 μg/g and/or normal fecal lactoferrin and/or normal CRP
claims.outcome: Ruling out active inflammation; avoiding endoscopy
claims.limitations: Conditional recommendation. 150 μg/g is a guideline decision threshold, not a diagnostic cut-off for an individual; calprotectin assays are not interchangeable and vary within-day / within-stool.
claims.conflictsWithExistingEvidence: Threshold granularity differs from STRIDE-II (SRC-033), which frames fecal-marker normalisation as a target without stating a numeric cut-off in its abstract. Not a contradiction; reconcile against full texts.
claims.regionalApplicabilityNote: US (AGA). Cut-off needs local assay validation in Canada.
